**3.2** **Numerical Method**

For the flow analysis and the estimation of the pump
performance, a numerical analysis was performed using
the commercial software ANSYS CFX, which numerically
solves the Navier–Stokes equations based on the finite element method. Steady-state analysis was performed using
cold-water, LN2, and LCH4 as working fluid. The condition
for numerical analysis is shown in Table 4.

The turbulence model is the shear stress transport k-omega
(SST k-ω), which is a hybrid turbulence model combining
the advantages of the standard k-ω and k-ε model. It has been
widely used to predict flow in centrifugal pumps and inducers
since it is found to be applicable for the accurate prediction
of flow under adverse pressure gradient and accounts for the
transport of the turbulence shear stress [24–26]. Inlet and
outlet boundary conditions are pressure and mass flow rate,
respectively. Free slip and no-slip condition were used for
boundary conditions of wall and impeller, respectively. The
mesh was generated as a polyhedron with an inflation layer
of 5. Figures 5 and 6 show the mesh of the pump assembly,
impeller, and inflation layer, respectively. In order to select
